rows.speaker: بعض العارفين
rows.claim: Some spiritual knowledges belong only to prophets; a Miʿraj report says God gave Muhammad knowledge of earlier and later peoples, secret knowledge only he could bear, chosen knowledge, the Qur'an, and commands to convey publicly.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعض العارفين أن من العلوم ما لا يعلمه إلا النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God also possesses knowledge He has reserved for Himself and revealed to none of creation.
rows.anchor: ولله تعالى علم استأثر به عز وجل لم يطلع عليه أحدا من خلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' request to learn guidance from Khidr occurred as a divine trial, as discussed earlier.
rows.anchor: قاله عن ابتلاء إلهي كما قدمنا

rows.speaker: فارس
rows.claim: Faris says Moses knew more of what he received from God, while Khidr knew more of what came to Moses.
rows.anchor: وقال فارس كما في أسرار القرآن : إن موسى عليه السلام كان أعلم من الخضر

rows.speaker: فارس
rows.claim: Faris also contrasts Moses as remaining through God with Khidr as annihilated through God.
rows.anchor: وقال أيضا : إن موسى كان باقيا بالحق والخضر كان فانيا بالحق

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says Khidr feared accompanying Moses because Moses was the most honored person of his time and intensely quick-tempered.
rows.anchor: قيل : علم الخضر أن موسى عليه السلام أكرم الخلق على الله تعالى في زمانه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say Khidr made Moses despair of himself so that companionship with Khidr would not distract him from companionship with God.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : آيسه من نفسه لئلا يشغله صحبته عن صحبة الحق

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say Moses would have been granted patience had he spoken like the sacrificial son; that wording more humbly entrusts success to God and calls himself one among the patient.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : لو قال كما قال الذبيح عليه السلام : ( ستجدني إن شاء الله من الصابرين )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asking the village for food involves humbling oneself but does not contradict reliance on God or earning a livelihood.
rows.anchor: سلكا طريق السؤال الذي يتعلق بذل النفس في الطريقة وهو لا ينافي التوكل وكذا الكسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses proposed a wage to spare them from begging the vile villagers; this reflects attention to means, a trait of the perfected, and signals that Moses was more complete than Khidr.
rows.anchor: أراد دفع ما أحوجهما من السؤال من أولئك اللئام وفيه نظر إلى الأسباب

rows.speaker: النصر أبادي
rows.claim: Al-Nasrabadhi says Khidr ended the companionship after Moses reached the limit of discipline but not Khidr's knowledge, lest further questions expose Moses.
rows.anchor: وقال النصر أبادي : لما علم الخضر بلوغ موسى إلى منتهى التأديب وقصور علمه عن علمه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Khidr feared Moses would ask about divine secrets of attributes and essence, which Khidr could not answer, so he said what he said.
rows.anchor: وقيل : خاف أن يسأله عن أسرار العلوم الربانية الصفاتية الذاتية فيعجز عن جوابه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The boy was exceptionally handsome and deeply loved by his parents, so Khidr feared he would become a trial for them.
rows.anchor: قيل : كان حسن الوجه جدا وكان محبوبا في الغاية لوالديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent predestination problem is answered by saying God decreed that the parents remain faithful if the boy were killed, and the killing preserved that outcome.
rows.anchor: بأن المقدر بقاؤهما على الإيمان إن قتل وقتله ليبقيا على ذلك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another answer is that a decree may change in its relation, without change in God's attribute itself; the discussion is linked to 13:39.
rows.anchor: موقيل إن المقدر قد يغير ولا يلزم من ذلك سوى التغير في تعلق صفته تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To the objection that guidance could remove the danger without killing, the answer is that the boy seemed unready for it, making that alternative contrary to wisdom.
rows.anchor: وأجيب بأن الظاهر أنه غير مستعد لذلك فهو مناف للحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr saw that Moses was about to contest the matter, so he closed off debate by saying he acted only on God's command, who is not questioned for what He commands and does.
rows.anchor: فتخلص من ذلك بقوله ( وما فعلته عن أمري ) أي بل فعلته بأمر الله عز وجل ولا يسئل سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr's bird-pecking metaphor was meant to shut down objections; knowledge of such matters may be among what God alone reserves.
rows.anchor: حين نقر العصفور في البحر سد لباب المناقشة

rows.speaker: النيسابوري
rows.claim: An esoteric reading maps the story onto spiritual psychology: seas and rock to master, disciple, and self; fish to a heart salted by worldly love; ship to law; boy to the commanding soul; village and wall to body, faculties, and the barrier to intelligible realities; treasure to intellectual and practical perfection guided by a shaykh.
rows.anchor: وأول بعضهم مجمع البحرين بمجمع ولاية الشيخ وولاية المريد والصخرة بالنفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited allegory is the interpretation chosen by al-Nisaburi; another interpreter offered an even stranger one.
rows.anchor: وهذا ما اختاره النيسابوري واختار غيره تأويلا آخر هو أدهى منه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The famous account says Quraysh asked about Dhul-Qarnayn after Jews prompted them; another says the Jews themselves were the questioners.
rows.anchor: السائلون في المشهور قريش بتلقين اليهود وقيل : اليهود أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most reports indicate the verse came after their question; the present tense evokes the earlier scene and its strangeness given what they had witnessed of the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وأكثر الآثار تدل على أن الآية نزلت بعد سؤالهم فالتعبير بصيغة الاستقبال لاستحضار الصورة الماضية

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation of the present tense is that it depicts the questioners as persisting while awaiting the answer.
rows.anchor: وقيل : للدلالة على استمرارهم على السؤال إلى وردود الجواب

rows.speaker: عقبة بن عامر
rows.claim: Uqba reports that people of Scripture sought the Prophet, who first said he did not know what they asked; after ablution and two prayers he welcomed them and offered to answer their question or another.
rows.anchor: فعن عقبة بن عامر قال : إن نفرا من أهل الكتاب جاؤا بالصحف أو الكتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although some reports imply revelation preceded the question, the majority view is that it followed it, and this Uqba report is not established as sound.
rows.anchor: والجمهور على الأول ولم تثبت صحة هذا الخبر

rows.speaker: جبير بن نفير
rows.claim: One view identifies Dhul-Qarnayn as a king God sent down to earth and gave every means; this is reported from Jubayr ibn Nufayr.
rows.anchor: فقيل : هو ملك أهبطه الله تعالى إلى الأرض وآتاه من كل شيء سببا وروى ذلك عن جبير بن نفير

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: A report says Umar objected to a man calling someone Dhul-Qarnayn, saying people use prophets' names but should not use angels' names; the author calls it strange and nearly unsound.
rows.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله تعالى عنه أنه سمع رجلا ينادي بمنى يا ذا القرنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if Umar's report were sound, it would not prove Dhul-Qarnayn was an angel; it could merely forbid that name because angels bear it, or refer to someone earlier given it.
rows.anchor: والخبر على فرض صحته ليس نصا في ذلك إذ يحتمل ولو على بعد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view calls him a righteous servant whom God made ruler over the earth and gave knowledge, wisdom, and awe, while his identity remains unknown.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو عبد صالح ملكه الله تعالى الأرض وأعطاه العلم والحكمة وألبسه الهيبة ولا نعرف من هو

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: One explanation says he was struck on the right horn, died, was revived and preached, then was struck on the left and revived; this is reported from Ali.
rows.anchor: الأول أنه دعا إلى طاعة الله تعالى فضرب على قرنه الأيمن فمات ثم بعثه الله تعالى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A second proposed origin of the name is that two generations of people died during his lifetime.
rows.anchor: الثاني أنه انقرض في وقته قرنان من الناس

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: A third explanation says the two sides of his head were made of copper; this is reported from Wahb ibn Munabbih.
rows.anchor: الثالث أنه كانت صفحتا رأسه من نحاس وروي ذلك عن وهب بن منبه

rows.speaker: عبيد بن يعلى
rows.claim: A fourth view gives him two hoof-like horns and says he was the first to wear a turban to conceal them; reported from Ubayd ibn Yaʿla.
rows.anchor: الرابع أنه كان في رأسه قرنان كالظلفين وهو أول من لبس العمامة ليسترهما

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A fifth proposed explanation is that his crown had two horns.
rows.anchor: الخامس أنه كان لتاجه قرنان

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A sixth explanation says he traversed the world's east and west, and this account is attributed to a raised prophetic report.
rows.anchor: السادس أنه طاف في الدنيا أي شرقها وغربها وروي ذلك مرفوعا

rows.speaker: قتادة ويونس بن عبيد
rows.claim: A seventh explanation says he had two long locks; this is reported from Qatada and Yunus ibn Ubayd.
rows.anchor: السابع أنه كان له غديرتان وروي ذلك عن قتادة ويونس بن عبيد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An eighth explanation says light and darkness were subjected to him: light guided him ahead while darkness stretched behind.
rows.anchor: الثامن أنه سخر له النور والظلمة فإذا سرى يهديه النور من أمامه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A ninth explanation says he entered both light and darkness.
rows.anchor: والتاسع أنه دخل النور والظلمة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A tenth explanation says he dreamed of ascending to the sun and taking hold of its two horns.
rows.anchor: العاشر أنه رأى في منامه كأنه صعد إلى الشمس وأخذ بقرنيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An eleventh possibility is an epithet for bravery, as if he butted his peers; Ardshir Bahman was similarly called long-handed for extending his rule.
rows.anchor: الحادي عشر أنه يجوز أن يكون قد لقب بذلك لشجاعته كأنه ينطح أقرانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author doubts that a ruler famed for dominion across the earth could be unidentified and judges some proposed name explanations nearly unsound.
rows.anchor: ولا يخفى أنه يبعد عدم معرفة رجل مكر له ما مكن في الأرض

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another identification makes him Fereydun son of Athfiyan son of Jamshid, fifth of the Persian Pishdadian kings, a just and obedient ruler.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو فريدون بن اثفيان بن جمشيد خامس ملوك الفرس

rows.speaker: أبو زيد البلخي
rows.claim: The book Ṣuwar al-Aqālīm says Dhul-Qarnayn was supported by revelation.
rows.anchor: وفي كتاب صورالأقاليم لأبي زيد البلخي أنه كان مؤيدا بالوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: General histories say he ruled the earth, divided it among his three sons Irag, Salm, and Tur with regions assigned to each, and set three governing codes called siyāsa, glossed as Greek for three laws.
rows.anchor: وفي عامة التاريخ أنه ملك الأرض وقسمها بين بنيه الثلاثة ايرج وسلم وتور

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: His name is explained by rule over the world's two ends, a reign of five hundred years in Rawdat al-Safa, or great bravery and conquest.
rows.anchor: ووجه تسميته ذا القرنين أنه ملك طرفي الدنيا أو طول أيام سلطنته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This identification is challenged because historians agree he did not travel east or west; Kawa the blacksmith conquered the lands, and no histories place Khidr at his vanguard as the popular account claims.
rows.anchor: قد أجمع أهل التاريخ على أنه لم يسافر لا شرقا ولا غربا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The response that proponents simply credit Alexander with all Quranic and reported deeds despite historians omitting them is, in the author's view, unpersuasive.
rows.anchor: وهو كما ترى

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir gives Alexander a long genealogy through Philip, Macedonian royalty, and ultimately Isaac and Abraham, placing his throne in Macedon and describing his conquests.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن كثير : هو ابن فيليس بن مصريم بن هرمس بن ميطون

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One disputed genealogy says Alexander was Philip's son, while another makes him Darius the Great's son through a rejected wife; the author calls the latter claim false.
rows.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أنه أبوه وذلك أنه تزوج بنت فيلقوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story that the dying Darius called Alexander brother and asked who attacked him is false; brother may simply be an honorific address between peers.
rows.anchor: وهو زعم باطل وقوله : يا أخي من باب الإكرام ومخاطبة الأمثال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alexander may be called Dhul-Qarnayn because he ruled the world's two ends or because of his bravery.
rows.anchor: وإنما سمي ذا القرنين لملكه طرفي الأرض أو لشجاعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran's account of reaching the far west, east, and north, together with historians' identification of Alexander as the ruler reaching that extent, is offered for the Greek Alexander identification.
rows.anchor: بأن القرآن دل على أن الرجل بلغ ملكه إلى أقصى المغرب وأقصى المشرق وجهة الشمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage recounts Alexander's campaigns through the Mediterranean, Egypt, Jerusalem, Armenia, Iraq, Persia, India, and China as evidence for this identification.
rows.anchor: وذلك لأنه لما مات أبوه جمع ملوك الروم والمغرب وقهرهم وانتهى إلى البحر الأخضر

rows.speaker: كاتب جلبي
rows.claim: Katib Çelebi objects that reliable histories do not establish Alexander's travel toward the west.
rows.anchor: واعترض أيضا بأن اسكندر المذكور لم يتحقق له سفر نحو المغرب في كتب التواريخ المعتبرة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies Dhul-Qarnayn with the earlier Roman Alexander, called the greater Dhul-Qarnayn, and gives several competing names and genealogies, including descent from Japheth or Qahtan.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو الاسكندر الرومي وهو متقدم على اليوناني بكثير ويقال له : ذو القرنين الأكبر

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: Some researchers say both Roman and Greek Alexander names refer to the conqueror of Darius; the Roman era is also called Syriac and Persian, with competing dates for its start.
rows.anchor: وذهب بعض المحققين إلى أن الإسكندر اليوناني والإسكندر الرومي كلاهما يطلقان على غالب دارا الأصغر

rows.speaker: ابن أبي الشكر
rows.claim: Some attribute the era to Solon son of al-Tabukhus, builder of Antioch; Ibn Abi al-Shukr confirms that attribution, while others suspend judgment because evidence conflicts.
rows.anchor: ينسبه إلى سولونس بن الطبوخوس الذي أمر ببناء أنطاكية وهو الذي صححه ابن أبي الشكر

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some deny that there were two Alexanders and say only one king conquered Darius and Persia; Dhul-Qarnayn might be him or someone else.
rows.anchor: ونفى بعضهم أن يكون في الزمن المتقدم بين الملوك اسكندران

rows.speaker: الكثير
rows.claim: Most say there were two Alexanders separated by about two thousand years, and the earlier, called Roman or Greek, is Dhul-Qarnayn; extravagant lifespans reported for him are all unreliable.
rows.anchor: والذي عليه الكثير أن المسمى بالإسكندر بين الملوك السالفة اثنان بينهما نحو ألفي سنة

rows.speaker: أبو الريحان البيروني
rows.claim: Al-Biruni identifies Dhul-Qarnayn as the Himyarite Abu Karib Shamir ibn Umayr ibn Afrikis, citing a poem by the Yemeni Tubbaʿ who calls him his Muslim grandfather and describes his east-west reach.
rows.anchor: أن ذا القرنين هو أبو كرب سمي بن عمير بن أفريقيس الحميري

rows.speaker: كاتب جلبي
rows.claim: Al-Biruni says this Yemeni identification seems closer because Yemen had many kings with Dhu-names; Katib Çelebi also chose it and placed Dhul-Qarnayn in Abraham's era.
rows.anchor: ويشبه أن يكون هذا القول أقرب لأن الأدواء كانوا من اليمن

rows.speaker: الأزرقي
rows.claim: Al-Azraqi says Dhul-Qarnayn accepted Islam at Abraham's hands, circumambulated the Kaaba with Abraham and Ishmael, and was welcomed and blessed by Abraham.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر الأزرقي أنه أسلم على يده عليه السلام وطاف معه بالكعبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Abraham offered Dhul-Qarnayn a horse, but he refused to ride in the city of the Friend; a cloud was then subjected to carry him and his army, as Abraham had foretold.
rows.anchor: أتي بفرس ليركب فقال : لا أركب في بلد فيه الخليل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alexander may be a Greek title meaning a good human; a Qahtanite genealogy could refer to the Yemeni rather than Roman or Greek ruler, with the transmitter confusing them.
rows.anchor: وذكر أنه يمكن أن يكون اسكندر لقبا لمن ذكر معربا عن الكسندر ومعناه في اللغة اليونانية آدمي جيد

rows.speaker: يعقوب بن إسحاق الكندي
rows.claim: Al-Kindi said Yunān was Qahtan's brother; Abu al-Abbas al-Nashi refuted this in a poem, and histories say Yemen's kings descended from Qahtan.
rows.anchor: نعم ذكر يعقوب بن إسحاق الكندي أن يونان أخو قحطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reliable histories do not list Abu Karib Shamir ibn Umayr ibn Afrikis among Yemen's kings, but do mention Shamir ibn Afrikis; Umayr may be a corruption of Shamir or Yarʿash.
rows.anchor: أنه لم يوجد في كتب التواريخ المعتبرة سمي ابن عمير بن أفريقيس

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some identify Shamir Yarʿash as Dhul-Qarnayn; Afrikis campaigned west, moved Berbers, founded Africa, and campaigned east, while Samarkand's name was glossed as Shamir-kand.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر بعضهم فيه أنه ذو القرنين وقالوا : إنه يقال له شمر يرعش

rows.speaker: دعبل الخزاعي
rows.claim: Daʿbal al-Khuzaʿi's poem credits Yemen's kings with writing at Marw and al-Shash and naming Samarkand; Shamir's rule length varies among historians, and his two locks explain the epithet.
rows.anchor: وإلى ذلك يشير دعبل الخزاعي بقوله يفتخر بملوك اليمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Shamir account confuses him with Abu Karib, actually Asʿad ibn Kulaykarib, whom some say believed in Muhammad before his mission and whose son Hassan killed him.
rows.anchor: ثم إن هذا لم يكن بأبي كرب وإنما المكنى به على ما رأيناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Neither Shamir nor Abu Karib can be the Dhul-Qarnayn who met Abraham: Shamir ruled after Solomon's era, while Abu Karib was later, lacked the title, and had no east-west conquests attributed to him.
rows.anchor: ولا يخفى أن كلا هذين الشخصين لا يصح أن يكون المراد بذي القرنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report placing Shamir in Moses' time also cannot identify him with the earlier Dhul-Qarnayn.
rows.anchor: وعليه أيضا لا يمكن أن يكون شمر هذا هو ذا القرنين السابق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Yemeni histories are discarded as contradictory but Dhul-Qarnayn is placed with Abraham, the competing universal rulers Fereydun, a Tubbaʿ, and Alexander cannot all have ruled the inhabited world then; only one could.
rows.anchor: والحاصل أن القول بأن فريدون كان في ذلك الزمان وكان مالكا المعمورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the world's two believing rulers were Solomon and Dhul-Qarnayn, and its two unbelieving rulers Nimrod and Nebuchadnezzar; placing Dhul-Qarnayn with Abraham requires their reigns to be successive, which the author finds strained.
rows.anchor: وقد جاء ملك الدنيا مؤمنان وكافران أما المؤمنان فسليمان عليه السلام وذو القرنين

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some books say Dhul-Qarnayn ruled after Nimrod, resolving the chronological problem.
rows.anchor: ورأيت في بعض الكتب القول بأن ذا القرنين ملك بعد نمرود

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say histories require rejecting or interpreting the report, since they do not give Solomon, Nimrod, or Nebuchadnezzar universal rule; the author considers the report likely unsound.
rows.anchor: والظاهر عدم الصحة

rows.speaker: اليهود
rows.claim: An objection says the Jews' Torah does not mention Dhul-Qarnayn; an Ibn Abi Hatim report from al-Suddi instead has Jews ask about a prophet named there only once, and answer that it was Dhul-Qarnayn.
rows.anchor: فقد أخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن السدي أن اليهود قالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the question itself implies Dhul-Qarnayn appeared in their scripture, and modern Jewish denial should be disregarded; absence from the Torah is only an improbability, not a strong objection.
rows.anchor: بل الظاهر من سؤالهم أن له ذكرا في كتابهم وإنكارهم اليوم ذلك لا يلتفت إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No proposed identification of Dhul-Qarnayn is free from conflicting reports and speculation.
rows.anchor: هذا وبالجملة لا يكاد يسلم في أمر ذي القرنين شيء من الأقوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author favors Alexander son of Philip, conqueror of Darius, identified as Greek or Roman Alexander, and regards him as a believer who committed no unbelief in creed, speech, or deed.
rows.anchor: تختار أنه الإسكندر بن فليقوس غالب دارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Studying under Aristotle does not establish agreement with all his teachings; teachers and pupils can sharply disagree, as Moses, al-Ashʿari, and Aristotle's disagreement with Plato illustrate.
rows.anchor: إن تلمذته على أرسطو لا تمنع من ذلك

rows.speaker: صدر الدين الشيرازي
rows.claim: Mulla Sadra says Aristotle was a monotheist worshipper who affirmed the world's origination and eventual destruction, citing 21:104; claims otherwise stem from misunderstanding Aristotle and other philosophers.
rows.anchor: أن الملا صدر الدين الشيرازي ذكر أن أرسطو كان حكيما عابدا موحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author does not accept that Alexander never traveled west or that Khidr's lack of documented ministerial service disproves the identification; Khidr may have served another ruler of that name.
rows.anchor: ولا نسلم عدم سفره نحو المغرب ولا ثبوت أن الخضر كان وزير ذي القرنين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Khidr may have been among Alexander's wise men and served as a minister, known then as a sage rather than a prophet; lack of historians' mention does not prove absence.
rows.anchor: وقيل : يمكن أن يكون عليه السلام في جملة الحكماء الذين معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ministerial service could mean managing and supporting the affairs of a righteous non-prophet king; a prophet's assistance to a just ruler is not objectionable and occurred among the Israelites.
rows.anchor: المراد من وزارته له تدبير أموره ونصرته ولا ضرر في نصرة نبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Choosing a Yemeni king or another Alexander requires placing him outside Abraham's era or after/alongside Nimrod as his subordinate, and setting aside the histories, as one must for Fereydun.
rows.anchor: فإن اخترت أنه من ملوك اليمن أو اسكندر آخر يلزمك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because wholesale rejection of diverse historical records is difficult, the author says the most useful choice in debate with other religions is Alexander son of Philip, conqueror of Darius.
rows.anchor: والأقرب عندي لإلزام أهل الملل والنحل الضالين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says Jews share this identification yet insult Alexander, despite accounts that he honored them and their Jerusalem priests.
rows.anchor: واليهود قاطبة على هذا لكنهم لعنهم الله تعالى وقعوا في الإسكندر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question concerns Dhul-Qarnayn's story, not his person or essence.
rows.anchor: ثم إن السؤال ليس عن ذات ذي القرنين بل عن شأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the answer, من is partitive and منه refers to Dhul-Qarnayn: the Prophet will recount some of his reports; alternatively, the pronoun refers to God and من marks the source, meaning Quran.
rows.anchor: والهاء لذي القرنين ومن تبعيضية والمراد من أنبائه وقصصه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The future particle سـ signals certainty and fulfillment of the promise, not future timing, since the verse was revealed connected to the rest of the story; a poem illustrates this usage.
rows.anchor: والسين للتأكيد والدلالة على التحقق المناسب لتقدم تأييده صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تمكين here means enabling him and preparing the means; تمكينه may mean making him capable, while تمكين له means granting capacity and strength, though the expressions overlap.
rows.anchor: والتمكين ههنا الاقدار وتمهيد الأسباب يقال مكنه ومكن له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His earthly power involved administration and judgment, many troops, awe, and dignity; it could also be read as deriving from place, with either expression yielding a similar sense.
rows.anchor: من حيث التدبير والرأي وكثرة الجنود والهيبة والوقار

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One report says God enabled him through a subjugated cloud, means of travel, and light, so day and night were equal for him; the author says the report seems unsound.
rows.anchor: وقيل : تمكينه في الأرض من حيث أنه سخر له السحاب ومد له في الأسباب

rows.speaker: مقاتل والضحاك
rows.claim: Another view says his empowerment was through prophethood and miracles; this is reported by Abu al-Shaykh from Abu al-Warqa and adopted by Muqatil and al-Dahhak.
rows.anchor: وقيل : تمكينه بالنبوة وإجراء المعجزات

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: A report from Ali, through Abu al-Fadl, says Dhul-Qarnayn was neither prophet nor king, but a righteous servant who loved and advised God and was loved and supported.
rows.anchor: ولكن كان عبدا صالحا أحب الله تعالى فأحبه ونصح الله تعالى فنصحه

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says Dhul-Qarnayn reached the two barriers and was a warner, but he had heard no reliable report that Dhul-Qarnayn was a prophet.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن ابن زيد أنه قال : ذو القرنين بلغ السدين وكان نذيرا

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority say Dhul-Qarnayn was not a prophet; some suspend judgment because Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying he did not know whether Dhul-Qarnayn was a prophet, with al-Hakim grading the report authentic.
rows.anchor: وإلى أنه ليس بنبي ذهب الجمهور وتوقف بعضهم لما أخرجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's statement of not knowing need not have remained his final view; he may later have learned Dhul-Qarnayn was not a prophet, as Ali's report indicates.
rows.anchor: أن هذا النفي لم يكن ليستمر لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The means granted to him were every route to his royal aims—knowledge, power, or tools—not knowledge alone; من may explain سبب, with some proposing a causal reading requiring no ellipsis.
rows.anchor: أي طريقا يوصله إليه وهو كل ما يتوصل به إلى المقصود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not prove that Dhul-Qarnayn was a prophet, despite the argument made by some.
rows.anchor: واستدل بعض من قال بنبوته بالآية على ذلك وليس بشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa is explicative: he intended to reach the west, then followed a means that would take him there.
rows.anchor: والتقدير فأراد بلوغ المغرب فأتبع

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: He may have set out west first because it was nearer, or to follow the sun's motion; this does not mean west is better than east.
rows.anchor: ولعل قصد بلوغ المغرب ابتداء لأنه أقرب إليه وقيل : لمراعاة الحركة الشمسية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Suyuti says there is no conclusive evidence that one direction is superior to the other.
rows.anchor: لا قطع بتفضيل إحدى الجهتين على الأخرى لتعارض الأدلة

rows.speaker: نافع وابن كثير
rows.claim: Nafi and Ibn Kathir read أتبع with hamzat al-wasl and doubled ت, as in the later occurrence; some consider both readings synonymous and taking one object.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن كثير ( فأتبع ) بهمزة الوصل وتشديد التاء

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd distinguishes وصل اتبع as following along a route from قطع أتبع as catching up, as in 28:42 and 37:10.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيد اتبع بالوصل في السير وأتبع بالقطع معناه اللحاق

rows.speaker: يونس
rows.claim: Yunus says أتبع with hamza means rapid, urgent pursuit, while اتبع without it means simply moving on and following.
rows.anchor: وقال يونس : ( أتبع ) بالقطع للمجد المسرع الحثيث الطلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhul-Qarnayn reached the inhabited world's western limit, apparently stopping at the western encircling sea, Oceanus, near the Fortunate Isles.
rows.anchor: منتهى الأرض من جهة المغرب بحيث لا يتمكن أحد من مجاوزته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حمئة means having black mud, from the verb for a well becoming full of mud.
rows.anchor: أي ذات حمأة وهي الطين الأسود من حمئت البئر تحمأ حمأ

rows.speaker: عبد الله وطلحة بن عبيد الله وعمرو بن العاص
rows.claim: A group of Companions, Ibn Amir, Hamza, and al-Kisa'i read حامية, meaning hot; Ibn Abbas initially rejected that reading.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله وطلحة بن عبيد الله وعمرو بن العاص

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In a report via Uthman ibn Hadhir, Ibn Abbas insisted on حمئة when told Muawiya read حامية; Muawiya consulted Abdullah ibn Amr and Kaʿb about the Torah, where Kaʿb found no sun setting in water and mud.
rows.anchor: أن ابن عباس ذكر له أن معاوية قرأ ( في عين حامية ) فقال له : ما نقرؤها إلا ( حمئة )

rows.speaker: ابن أبي حاضر
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Hadhir cites Tubbaʿ's poem: the sun sets in a spring of mud; he glosses خلب as mud, ثأط as mud, and حرمد as black, prompting Ibn Abbas to have it written down.
rows.anchor: قول تبع فيما ذكر به ذا القرنين في كلفه بالعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The readings need not conflict because the spring could be both hot and muddy; although a hamza-to-yā shift is proposed, the Ibn Abbas-Muawiya exchange weighs against it, so the apparent preference is Ibn Abbas's reading.
rows.anchor: وظاهر ما سمعت ترجيح قراءة ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: A sound-graded report says Abu Dharr rode behind the Prophet on a donkey and heard him say the sun sets in a hot spring, supporting Muawiya's reading and linking في عين to تغرب.
rows.anchor: نعم ما أخرجه ابن أبي شيبة وعبد بن حميد وابن المنذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposal that في عين modifies وجدها as a circumstantial phrase is untenable; the sun only appears to set in water, as seen from a sea or broad flat land, and وجد may mean saw.
rows.anchor: وقول بعض المتعسفين بأنه متعلق بمحذوف وقع حالا من فاعل ( وجدها )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spring may be an actual spring by the sea or the sea itself, called an eye; compared with God's greatness, even the sea is a drop.
rows.anchor: ثم المراد بالعين الحمئة إما عين في البحر أو البحر نفسه

rows.speaker: بعض البغداديين
rows.claim: Some Baghdadis take في to mean عند, so the sun sets at a spring.
rows.anchor: وزعم بعض البغداديين أن ( في ) بمعنى عند أي تغرب عند عين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take the verse literally, and another says a fish swallows the sun; while affirming God's power, the author dismisses these as childish because sunrise and sunset vary across horizons and polar regions.
rows.anchor: ومثله ما نقله الطرطوشي من أنها يبلعها حوت بل هذا كلام لا يقبله إلا الصبيان

rows.speaker: إمام الحرمين
rows.claim: The sun continually rises for some people and sets for others according to their horizons; Imam al-Haramayn says there is no disagreement on this.
rows.anchor: بل قال إمام الحرمين : لا خلاف في ذلك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report says the sun, like a waterwheel, travels in the sky by day and beneath the earth at night until it rises in the east; the moon does likewise.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال الشمس بمنزلة الساقية تجري بالنهار في السماء

rows.speaker: خزيمة بن حكيم السلمي
rows.claim: Al-Zuhri reports that when Khuzaima asked the Prophet why water is hot in winter and cold in summer, he attributed it to the sun's longer or shorter journey beneath earth; the text notes this path varies by horizon and season.
rows.anchor: عن الزهري أن خزيمة بن حكيم السلمي سأل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the sun circles the sky after setting and returns east, but the author says this report is hardly sound.
rows.anchor: فما أخرجه أبو الشيخ عن الحسن قال : إذا غربت الشمس دارت في فلك السماء

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: A Bukhari report says the Prophet told Abu Dharr at sunset that the sun goes until it prostrates beneath the Throne, relating this to 36:38.
rows.anchor: ما أخرجه البخاري عن أبي ذر قال : كنت مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report can mean the sun descends beneath the earth to its lowest point, like prostration, or truly prostrates appropriately; under the Throne may designate a particular aligned place, since everything is otherwise beneath and within it.
rows.anchor: وأجيب بأن المراد أنها تذهب تحت الأرض حتى تصل إلى غاية الانحطاط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This explanation presumes a spherical firmament surrounding celestial bodies and defining directions, a philosophers' view; the sun reaches its lowest descent and rises again without leaving its orbit.
rows.anchor: وهذا مبني على أنه جسم كري محيط بسائر الأفلاك والفلكيات

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report says angels rapidly carry the sun to the seventh heaven, where it waits under the Throne for permission to rise and then descends through the heavens.
rows.anchor: فعن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أن الشمس إذا غربت رفع بها إلى السماء السابعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although God's power permits this, the report conflicts with simultaneous sunrise and sunset around the earth and six-month polar days or nights, so it may be unsound.
rows.anchor: إلا أنه لا يتسنى مع تحقق غروبها عند قوم وطلوعها عند آخرين

rows.speaker: الجلال السيوطي
rows.claim: Al-Suyuti explicitly says Abu al-Shaykh's report about the sun's ascent has a weak chain.
rows.anchor: وقد نص الجلال السيوطي على أن أبا الشيخ رواه بسند واه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Bukhari and Ibn Abi Shayba versions suggest Abu Dharr was asked twice; in the second response he deferred to God and the Prophet out of courtesy and a wish for further benefit.
rows.anchor: أن أبا ذر رضي الله تعالى عنه سئل مرتين إلا أنه رد العلم في الثانية

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: The people at the western spring wore predator skins and ate what the sea washed up; Wahb says they were the innumerable Nasik people.
rows.anchor: لباسهم على ما قيل : جلود السباع وطعامهم ما لفظه البحر

rows.speaker: أبو زيد السهيلي
rows.claim: Al-Suhayli says they descended from Thamud and lived in the twelve-gated city Jabarisa, also called Jargisa in Syriac; Ibn Jurayj reports similarly.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو زيد السهيلي : هم قوم من نسل ثمود كانوا يسكنون جابرسا

rows.speaker: ابن السائب
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sa'ib says the people included both believers and unbelievers, while the majority say they were unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وزعم ابن السائب أنه كان فيهم مؤمنون وكافرون والذي عليه الجمهور أنهم كانوا كفارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave Dhul-Qarnayn the choice to punish them by killing or treat them well by calling them to truth and guiding them toward reward; the latter wording subtly favors mercy.
rows.anchor: وفي التعبير بإما أن تتخذ فيهم حسنا دون إما أن تدعوهم مثلا إيماء إلى ترجيح الشق الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional clauses allow several grammatical parses, including nominative subject or predicate and accusative object, with analogous parses for treating them well.
rows.anchor: ومحل إن مع صلته إما الرفع على الابتداء أو على الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some infer prophethood from God's direct address; those denying it propose an angel, another prophet, or inspiration consistent with that prophet's law, but killing cannot rest on inspiration alone.
rows.anchor: واستدل بالآية من قال بنبوته والقول عند بعضهم بواسطة ملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appeal to Abraham's dream of sacrificing his son does not weaken the argument because prophets' dreams and inspirations are revelation; the verse strongly indicates Dhul-Qarnayn's prophethood, perhaps through another prophet.
rows.anchor: وفيه أن رؤيا الأنبياء عليهم السلام وإلهاماتهم وحي

rows.speaker: علي بن عيسى
rows.claim: Ali ibn Isa's gloss that God said to Muhammad that his companions said this, with the speech omitted because Dhul-Qarnayn was not a prophet, is highly strained; attributing courtiers' deliberation to God is similarly contrived.
rows.anchor: وقال علي بن عيسى : المعنى قلنا يا محمد قالوا أي جنده الذين كانوا معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhul-Qarnayn answers the prophet or his own close advisers after receiving God's direction, choosing the second option in the offered choice.
rows.anchor: ذو القرنين لذلك النبي أو لمن عنده من خواصه بعد أن تلقى أمره تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoer is one who wrongs himself through shirk and refuses the invitation; the apparent meaning is that he will be killed by the sword.
rows.anchor: أما من ظلم ( نفسه ولم يقبل دعوتي وأصر على ما كان عليه

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says they were put inside copper cattle and fire was lit beneath them until they were torn apart; the author considers this unlikely to be sound.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن السدي قال : كان عذابه أن يجعلهم في بقر من صفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The royal plural attributes punishment to Dhul-Qarnayn as its cause and commander, not as the direct executioner; interpreting the pronoun as shared by God and himself is also unlikely and raises a problem of associating another with God.
rows.anchor: وأتى بنون العظمة على عادة الملوك وإسناد التعذيب إليه لأنه السبب الآمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sinner is returned to his Lord in the afterlife for a terrible, abhorrent punishment in Hell; عذابا functions as an accusative verbal noun for يعذبه or is governed by both verbs.
rows.anchor: أي منكرا فظيعا وهو العذاب في نار جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying returned to his Lord rather than to you indicates the earlier exchange was not revelation addressed directly to Dhul-Qarnayn but speech with a prophet or his close advisers.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله ( إلى ربه ) دون إليك دلالة على أن الخطاب السابق لم يكن بطريق الوحي إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer follows the invitation and does righteous deeds; his good recompense in both worlds means the best reward, good deed, or Paradise, with several grammatical analyses of جزاء الحسنى.
rows.anchor: أي فله المثوبة الحسنى أو الفعلة الحسنى أو الجنة

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن
rows.claim: Abu al-Hasan objects that Arabs scarcely use a circumstantial phrase fronted in this way except in poetry; al-Farra' instead calls it a specification.
rows.anchor: وتعقب ذلك أبو الحسن بأنه لا تكاد العرب تتكلم بالحال مقدما

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومسروق
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Masruq read جزاء in the accusative without tanwin; al-Mahdawi explains deletion at a meeting of two vowelless sounds, while others posit genitive construction and an implied subject.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس ومسروق ( جزاء ) منصوبا غير منون

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي إسحاق
rows.claim: Abdullah ibn Abi Ishaq reads جزاء nominative with tanwin, as the subject with الحسنى in apposition and a prepositional predicate.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله بن أبي إسحاق بالرفع والتنوين

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Other canonical readers have nominative without tanwin; Abu Ali explains the construct as reward for good deeds or Paradise, as in دار الآخرة.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي : والمراد على الإضافة جزاء الخلال الحسنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusra means something easy and facilitated, with ذَا omitted; the verbal noun is used emphatically, and Abu Jaʿfar reads it with two dammas wherever it occurs.
rows.anchor: أي سهلا ميسرا غير شاق وتقديره ذا يسر

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari interprets good treatment as taking them prisoner, making the choice killing or captivity; the response could distinguish killing or imprisonment for unbelievers from leaving believers except for required penalties.
rows.anchor: وقال الطبري : المراد من اتخاذ الحسن الأسر فيكون قد خير بين القتل والأسر

rows.speaker: الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf says both readings' word order has a rhetorical point: divine mercy is foregrounded to subordinate human action, while punishment follows the order of existence and escalates to intensify anger.
rows.anchor: وفي الكشف أنه روعي فيه على الوجهين نكتة بتقديم ما من الله تعالى في جانب الرحمة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The choice may distribute outcomes rather than offer alternatives: punish those who persist in wrongdoing and treat kindly those who repent.
rows.anchor: وجوز حمل ( إما أن تعذب وإما أن تتخذ ) على التوزيع دون التخيير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhul-Qarnayn then followed a route that led back from the western setting place toward the eastern rising place.
rows.anchor: أي طريقا راجعا من مغرب الشمس موصلا إلى مشرقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sunrise place means the first place the sun reaches in the inhabited world, its easternmost limit.
rows.anchor: يعني الموضع الذي تطلع عليه الشمس أولا من معمورة الأرض

rows.speaker: الحسن وعيسى وابن محيصن
rows.claim: They read مطلع with fatḥa; it is reported from Ibn Kathir and the Meccans. Researchers call it a verbal noun requiring an implied place, whereas al-Jawhari treats it as a place noun like the kasra reading.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وعيسى وابن محيصن ( مطلع ) بفتح اللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some morphology authorities allow مطلع, open or closed, for both place and time; researchers say the open form occurs as a verbal noun in eloquent speech, while Abu Hayyan calls the kasra pattern limited and anomalous.
rows.anchor: وقد صرح بعض أئمة التصريف أن المطلع جاء في المكان والزمان فتحا وكسرا

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa'i says the kasra-pattern verb was a language that died out among Arabs, although its form remains in the place and time noun.
rows.anchor: وكان الكسائي يقول : هذه لغة ماتت في كثير من لغات العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Given Dhul-Qarnayn's means, he apparently reached the east quickly; the claim that he took twelve years is unlikely unless he stopped during the journey.
rows.anchor: ثم أن الظاهر من حال ذي القرنين وكونه قد أوتي من كل شيء سببا أنه بلغ مطلع الشمس في مدة قليلة

rows.speaker: سمرة بن جندب
rows.claim: A report through Ibn Jurayj from Hasan and Samura says the people had no buildings and hid in underground passages when the sun rose.
rows.anchor: عن ابن جريج قال : حدثت عن الحسن عن سمرة بن جندب قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: A report attributed to Hasan says their land could not bear buildings, so they submerged in water at sunrise and emerged to graze like animals at sunset.
rows.anchor: وذكر أنه حديث سمرة أن أرضهم لا تحمل البناء

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Some say they had neither clothing nor buildings; Mujahid describes the Sudanese near sunrise as especially often unclothed, while other reports call them Zanj or Indians.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد من لا يلبس الثياب من السودان عند مطلع الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A traveler's elaborate story of an ear-clad people, the sun rising over water like oil, underground shelters, and sun-cooked fish is dismissed as granny tales for children; Wahb says the people were called Mansak.
rows.anchor: وأنت تعلم أن مثل هذه الحكايات لا ينبغي أن يلتفت إليها ويعول عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The negative wording appears to deny any shelter, conflicting with reports of tunnels; one answer says general expressions exclude rare shelters, though exclusion of rare cases is disputed.
rows.anchor: وظاهر الآية لوقوع النكرة فيها في سياق النفي يقتضي أنهم ليس لهم ما يسترهم أصلا

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya reads lack of a sun-shield as the sun's nearness and effect upon them by God's power; tunnels would otherwise count as a substantial covering.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية : الظاهر أن نفي جعل ساتر لهم من الشمس عبارة عن قربها إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author favors the literal absence of any covering until one of the earlier reports is established as authentic.
rows.anchor: وأنا أختار ذلك إلى أن تثبت صحة أحد الأخبار السابقة
